summary: SSE session rebind to incorrect backend during multipath handoff leads to interleaved system messages and clipped closing paragraph
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightWrite Labs reports repeated occurrences where Server-Sent Events (SSE) streams appear to receive interleaved 'system' messages from a different conversation and the final paragraph of the assistant response is missing. This happens after a network path migration (cellular->wifi or carrier multipath) which triggers a multipath handoff and session rebind.

Impact:
- Customer-facing LLM responses occasionally contain unrelated system messages mid-stream and lose the final closing paragraph (important for code blocks and policy footers).
- Affects a subset of long-running streams under prod us-east-1 for the customer's dedicated pool.
- Reproducible for ~6% of handoffs observed over the last 24h for this customer.

Environment:
- Prod: dedicated GPU pool (dedicated tier, BrightWrite account) in us-east-1.
- Edge: our edge-sidecar fleet (node pool es-rtf-us-east).
- Client: mobile web (PWA) with SSE fallback; network path migrations tested via Charles proxy.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a long generation (800-1200 token output) via SSE to rw-chat-v1 pinned on dedicated pool.
2) While streaming, trigger a network handoff (IPv6->IPv4 multipath or carrier switch).
3) Client reconnects and SSE receives a resume frame.
4) Stream resumes but contains an interleaved 'system' message and the last 1-2 paragraphs are missing.

Observed behavior:
- The stream shows a short run of tokens from a different recent session (system/assistant metadata), then resumes with the correct content but truncates the final closing paragraph.
- No 5xx from the serving runtime; gateway logs show two different worker IDs returning chunks for the same session-id during the handoff window.

Expected behavior:
- Exactly one backend worker continues the session after handoff; no mixing of content. The resumed stream should contain the full closing paragraphs.

Temporary workaround:
- Customer was advised to prefer websocket fallback for long-running streams while we investigate, and to set shorter keepalive probes on their mobile SDK to reduce probability of multipath.

2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE (Thomas Li) - Initial triage: saw two different worker IDs (worker-12 and worker-47) both stream-sending chunks within 150ms for same session-id during path migration. Gateway logs: 'session_lookup: cache_miss -> bind_to_worker(worker-47)'. Hypothesis: session mapping rebind race when ephemeral mapping is freed and reused during multipath stitch.

2026-03-10 13:22 - Engineer (Priya Sharma) - Reproduced locally with simulated multipath. Observed sidecar mapping table eviction at ~30s, and rebind code uses the ephemeral session token plus client-ip to key mapping; on path migration client-ip changed triggering a new bind before we drained previous worker's final buffer. Creating a patch to add a monotonic session epoch and drain handshake during rebind.

2026-03-11 02:15 - Engineer (Priya Sharma) - Deployed hotfix to edge-sidecar (v2.14.1) behind feature flag: enforce session epoch check and require previous worker to signal 'handoff-complete' or wait max 500ms before binding new worker. Rollout initiated to canary nodes in us-east-1.
2026-03-12 08:30 - Support (Maria Gomez) - Customer ran a controlled test and reported no interleaved system messages across 120 handoffs. Closing verification pending at 24h monitoring window.
investigation_notes:
Logs show that during multipath rebind the gateway sometimes rehashed session keys and immediately bound the session-id to a new worker while the old worker still had in-flight token buffers. The sidecar's session map eviction policy returned the mapping slot quickly; a new session epoch was not asserted in client resume frames so two workers treated resume as authoritative. Root cause: session binding was keyed insufficiently (ephemeral token + client-ip) and did not require a monotonic epoch or a drain handshake. The hotfix enforces an epoch in resume frames and a short drain window.
Referenced traces: trace-20260310-87a3 (worker-12 lastWrite at t, worker-47 firstWrite at t+120ms)
Impact estimate: affected ~0.5% of total handoffs cluster-wide, higher for clients undergoing IP family change.
resolution:
Deployed fix in edge-sidecar v2.14.1 (commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-sidecar/commit/3a7f2b9). Fix details:
- Require monotonic session_epoch on resume frames and reject resumes with older epochs.
- Add a negotiated 'drain-ack' handshake: old worker must ack final buffer or max-wait 500ms before new bind.
- Add observability: 'handoff_conflict' metric and per-session handoff_trace_id in logs.
Rollout: canary us-east-1 -> full us-east within 3 hours. Post-deployment monitoring for 48h showed no recurrence for BrightWrite and cohort tests down to <0.05% handoff anomalies.
Follow-up actions: 1) Update streaming runbook with handoff mitigation steps. 2) Add integration test covering IPv6->IPv4 multipath rebind. 3) Consider increasing default drain-wait to 1s for high-latency mobile clients (RFC to product).
